title: A locally free graded tail gives a flat projective family with its Hilbert polynomial
statement: Let $U$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $n\geq0$, and let $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_U[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/J$ for a quasi-coherent homogeneous ideal $J$ locally generated by finitely many homogeneous elements. The variables have degree one; $J$ may have degree-zero elements. Let $m\geq0$ and $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ satisfy $P(d)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ for $d\geq m$. Suppose that $\mathcal B_d$ is locally free of rank $P(d)$ for every $d\geq m$. Then the relative Proj $Z=\operatorname{Proj}_U\mathcal B$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented over $U$, and its geometric fibres have Hilbert polynomial $P$ for this embedding. For every $g:T\to U$, the coefficientwise pullback algebra defines the closed subscheme $Z\times_UT\subset\mathbf P^n_T$; its equations are the images of $J$ after tensor pullback. For a field $k$ and any finitely generated homogeneous ideal $I\subset k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$, the eventual Hilbert polynomial of $k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/I$ equals that of the closed subscheme $\operatorname{Proj}(k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/I)$ with its indicated embedding, without requiring $I$ to be saturated.

Relative Proj base change is the existing lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-polynomial-quotient-proj-presentation to the given quotient. It supplies the closed embedding over $U$, finite presentation, and, over every affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the cover $D_+(x_i)=\operatorname{Spec}B_{(x_i),0}$ with $B_d=\Gamma(V,\mathcal B_d)$. Degree-zero equations and empty charts are included.

proof.text: Each $\mathcal B_d$ for $d\geq m$ is finite locally free by hypothesis. Apply lem-sfb-locally-free-tail-chart-flatness on every $V$ and to each degree-one image $x_i$: every $B_{(x_i),0}$ is flat over $R$. By lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine the chart maps are flat. At a point of such a chart the local rings and structural map agree with those for $Z\to U$; the stalk definition of flatness therefore proves flatness everywhere.

proof.text: For any $g:T\to U$, apply lem-sfb-polynomial-quotient-proj-cartesian. Its image-ideal and cartesian-embedding assertions give exactly the requested coefficientwise equations and embedded base change, including nonflat $g$.

source.place: Agent-extracted interface for former proof step 6 of lem-sfb-flat-graded-tail-proj: Constructions Tag 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), canonical chart maps and their naturality for the graded polynomial quotient. The tensor-quotient and embedding compatibility arguments, not an additional abstract base-change theorem, are preserved in the report.

proof.text: First take any field $k$ and homogeneous ideal $I\subset k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$, and put $A=k[x]/I$. Apply lem-trf-standard-graded-hilbert-function with standard graded ring $S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ and finite graded $S$-module $M=A$ (generated by $1$, or zero if $I=(1)$). This gives a polynomial $Q$ eventually equal to $\dim_k A_d$. Apply lem-sfb-projective-coordinate-ring-euler-polynomial to this very ideal $I$. It gives $\dim_k A_d=\chi(\operatorname{Proj}A,\mathcal O(d))$ for all sufficiently large $d$. Thus $Q$ is exactly the Hilbert polynomial of the closed subscheme with its indicated embedding: the eventual graded and twisted Euler polynomials agree. This proves the field assertion for unsaturated ideals as well as saturated ones; irrelevant-primary ideals and the unit ideal give the empty scheme and zero polynomial. Using $S$ rather than requiring $A$ to be standard graded also avoids the false requirement $A_0=k$ in the zero-ring case.

source.place: Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module); varieties.tex Tag 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0); algebra.tex Tag 00K1 (proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial), all through the cited existing nodes

proof.text: Finally let $u\in U$ and $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(u)}$. Step 3 with $T=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ identifies the geometric fibre with the embedded Proj of $A=\mathcal B\otimes\Omega$, a quotient of $\Omega[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ by the image ideal. Degreewise coefficient pullback gives $A_d=(\mathcal B_d)_u\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U,u}}\Omega$. For each $d\geq m$, take a local free frame for $\mathcal B_d$ around $u$; tensoring that frame gives $A_d\cong\Omega^{P(d)}$, so $\dim_\Omega A_d=P(d)$. By step 4 the Hilbert polynomial $Q$ of this embedded geometric fibre eventually equals these dimensions, hence $Q(d)=P(d)$ for every sufficiently large integer $d$. A nonzero rational polynomial has only finitely many roots, so $Q=P$. This proves the fibre assertion, including $P=0$ and empty fibres, and completes all clauses.
